ModMetaData.name: Jawa Sea Shaper
ModMetaData.author: Mandrake
ModMetaData.description:
Shapes the planet's oceans at world generation: a quarter of the surface under water, in three torn bodies near the poles, with the coastlines left deliberately ragged.
Campaign tooling for a desert world, not general-purpose content. It changes worldgen only, and only on the surface layer.
WHAT IT DOES
RimWorld generates 43-55% ocean unaided, scattered wherever the elevation noise happens to fall below zero. This replaces that with a deliberate arrangement:
* ~25% of tiles under water (accepts 22-28%) * exactly THREE connected bodies, not a scatter * each body at high latitude, its centroid nearer a pole than the equator * each body oddly shaped rather than round
It is mostly a REMOVAL job. Most of the planet is raised out of the sea, and three patches are lowered into it.
HOW "ODDLY SHAPED" IS MEASURED, BECAUSE OTHERWISE IT IS NOT A REQUIREMENT
Perimeter squared divided by area. A circle scores 4*pi = 12.57, and that is the number to beat; every body must reach at least 25, i.e. twice as ragged as a circle of the same area.
This is the requirement most likely to be quietly failed, because every natural blob-growth algorithm trends round. So the sea is not grown as a disc. Each step claims the frontier tile standing highest in a Perlin field rather than the nearest one - invasion percolation - so growth follows the noise's ridges, throwing out peninsulas and leaving bays behind. Ranking rather than thresholding also fixes the quota exactly: a Perlin field is bell-shaped, so any fixed cut gives a water fraction that drifts with the seed.
WHAT IT WRITES, AND WHY BOTH HALVES MATTER
Every tile it touches gets BOTH a new elevation and a new biome.
RimWorld has no sea-level setting. SurfaceTile.WaterCovered is compiled as exactly "elevation <= 0" - so elevation IS the sea, and the biome label is only a label. A tile marked Ocean while carrying land elevation looks like sea on the map and behaves like dry ground; anything that goes underwater breaks on it. The reverse is equally broken. So both are always written together.
Tiles raised out of the water take their biome and elevation from their NEAREST ORIGINAL LAND NEIGHBOUR, by a breadth-first flood outward from every existing land tile.
This is a CONTINUITY rule, not a decision about the planet's biome mix. Raised beside badlands becomes badlands. Biomes are assigned by the vanilla Tiles step at order 5 and nothing re-runs it, so a raised tile that got no biome from us would stay labelled Ocean on dry ground. Copying the neighbour commits to nothing about which biomes the world should favour.
WHERE IT SITS IN WORLD GENERATION
Order 20 - after Terrain (0) and Tiles (5), before Lakes (150) and Rivers (200).
That ordering is the whole trick, and it is why this mod builds no rivers of its own. It finishes early enough that vanilla's river step runs afterwards, untouched, and carves rivers into the coastlines this step has just made. Verified against the shipped defs: nothing in the base game or its DLCs occupies any order between 5 and 150.
WHAT IT DELIBERATELY DOES NOT DO
* No coastline detailing, no per-body character, no shoreline art. * No change to the land biome mix beyond the continuity rule above. * No rivers, no lakes - it finishes and gets out of the way. * No unbounded loops. If a body cannot reach its quota the step logs the shortfall and stops. A world generation that hangs is worse than a sea that came out at 21%.
READING THE RESULT
The step logs one line reporting every acceptance test with a PASS or FAIL: the water fraction against the 22-28% band, the tile count, perimeter and compactness score of each body, each body's mean absolute latitude, and how many orphan tiles were released. Nothing is enforced by looping - the log line is the evidence, and the feature is judged by generating a few worlds and reading it.
Deterministic: the same world seed produces the same coastline every time.
